about: SDK 3.0.0 top-K (make_topk.py; the rule is api/layers_ref.py topk). Each case is one frame of log_probs: `bits` are the 38 float32 values as big-endian hex, `ranked` is the full ranking (ids, the log-probs as the doubles equal to the float32 values, the margins as doubles). With topK = k a frame holds the first k of each list. Test k 1, 2, 3 and 38. Compare ids and log-probs exactly and margins exactly: a margin that is off in the last place was not computed as a double.

cases.name: distinct
cases.why: 38 different values in a mixed order

cases.name: best_is_the_last_id
cases.why: values rise with the id: the best token is id 37

cases.name: blank_far_ahead
cases.why: blank near 0, the rest far below (most frames of a real take look like this)

cases.name: tie_at_the_top
cases.why: ids 5 and 9 share the best value: 5 comes first, its margin is 0

cases.name: tie_across_the_cut
cases.why: ranks 3 and 4 are equal: with k 3 the lower id is the one kept

cases.name: three_way_tie
cases.why: ranks 2, 3 and 4 are equal: ascending ids, two margins of 0

cases.name: flat
cases.why: all 38 equal (log of 1/38): ids 0 to 37 in order, every margin 0

cases.name: floor
cases.why: 8 values above a floor of 30 equal ones: the tail is the floor's ids in ascending order

cases.name: margin_needs_a_double
cases.why: the best is one float step below 0, the next is near -16.6: the difference is not a float32, so a margin computed in float is caught

cases.name: one_float_step_apart
cases.why: ids 4, 30 and 12 are one float32 step apart: the order follows the values, the margins are that step

cases.name: saturated
cases.why: a confident frame: blank at -2.4e-07, everything else below -15

cases.name: close_values
cases.why: 38 values within half a nat: no ties, small margins
